asOf: Historical observation dates stated per event
note: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed.

items.title: Warsaw
items.text: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939; the Soviet Union invaded from the east on 17 September. The Warsaw point locates the country’s capital, without inventing a partition or a daily front.

items.title: Nordic occupation
items.text: Denmark surrendered on 9 April 1940; Norway fought until 10 June. Follow national occupation status through Denmark’s main liberation date, 5 May 1945, and Norway’s capitulation, 8 May. Modern outlines are reference geography; Bornholm is an exception to Denmark’s main date.

items.title: Paris
items.text: Germany defeated France in June 1940. Occupied areas and the Vichy regime had different administrative arrangements. Paris locates the capital; this point does not fill all of France as one continuous occupied area.

items.title: Western Europe
items.text: The US Army’s Northern Europe atlas combines arrows dated from June 1944 to May 1945. Its geography is warped approximately onto this map for overview reading. Use opacity to compare; the arrows are a campaign summary, not one dated front.

items.title: Allied milestones
items.text: Use the dated slider to follow selected Allied milestones: Normandy on 6 June 1944, Paris on 25 August and Remagen on 7 March 1945. The joining line is schematic; it does not identify a single army’s route.

items.title: Bornholm
items.text: The Danish National Museum notes that Bornholm experienced Soviet bombardment during Denmark’s liberation. A country-level status colour cannot settle this island’s local control history. The point identifies the exception rather than drawing an unsupported control polygon.

occupationEvidence.precision: National status; Bornholm exception not mapped as a control polygon.
Surrender/occupation at national scale, not every island or local troop position.
